title: Global stocks build on tech-fuelled rally as oil retreats: Markets Wrap | Stock Market News
text:
The global stocks were on track for their best two-day gain in more than three months as a resurgent tech rally and a further decline in oil prices boosted sentiment.

The MSCI All Country World Index—the broadest measure of global equities—rose 0.4%, adding to Monday’s 2.2% advance. In Asia, South Korea’s chip-heavy Kospi Index rose 4.4% to be the top performer, followed by key gauges in Japan and Taiwan. That’s after US equity benchmarks on Monday capped their best session in about seven months, as dip buyers stepped in following last week’s tech-led selloff.

Futures for the S&P 500 Index rose 0.2% on Tuesday, while those for the Nasdaq 100 were little changed. European contracts climbed 0.9%.

Brent crude slipped further to trade below $92 a barrel after slumping almost 6% in the previous session to its lowest since August. President Donald Trump said further strikes on Iran wouldn’t be necessary, an indication that he’s winding down the conflict after the US midterm results underscored its unpopularity.

“The sharp drop in oil prices has given markets some much-needed breathing room. it’s eased some of the inflation pressure,” said Dilin Wu, a strategist at Pepperstone Group. “We still need to see whether buying interest can hold up. The selling may have eased, but the questions around AI spending and returns haven’t gone away.”

Global tech stocks are bouncing back following a tumultuous week that saw chipmakers bear the brunt of a selloff sparked by worries that the Democrats’ sweep of Congress in the US midterms may lead to tougher oversight of the artificial intelligence sector. The MSCI’s gauge of world equities finished last week at a six-month low.

The durability of the rebound remains in question though, with regulatory risks now layered on top of concerns that were already weighing on the AI sector—stretched valuations, soaring capital spending and uncertainty over the payoff from massive AI investments.

SoftBank Group Corp., the Tokyo-based backer of OpenAI Inc., reported its first net loss in almost two years on Tuesday after worries over AI spending and demand weighed on the tech investor’s top holdings.

Meanwhile, in one optimistic sign for the tech sector, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., the go-to chipmaker for Nvidia Corp. and Apple Inc., posted a 60% increase in October sales. Its shares finished at a one-week high.

Also, Anthropic PBC unveiled new versions of its powerful Mythos and Fable models, an effort to bolster its position as a leader in AI development on the eve of its long-awaited Wall Street debut. Separately, Reuters reported that the creator of the Claude chatbot sent out and retracted a filing that appeared to show it was aiming to raise as much as $69.3 billion ⁠through its IPO.

Earlier, the Nasdaq 100 rallied 3.4% on Monday while a gauge of chip stocks in the US surged nearly 7%. That’s even as shares of Nvidia slid 4.3% amid a probe into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after his admission of an affair with a woman identified in a series of reports as a suspected Chinese spy.

On the economic front, investors will be watching October US consumer prices data, which is slated to be released on Tuesday and is expected to show smaller increases than in September.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell one basis point to 4.87%. A gauge of the dollar was little changed after falling 0.5% on Monday.

“The Fed is uber-focused on inflation,” Carol Lye, portfolio manager and senior research analyst at Franklin Templeton, said on Bloomberg Television. “I suspect as inflation comes down, they may just possibly pause.”
